DATABASE SCHEMA
Table: CUSTOMERS
Purpose: Stores customer information.
Columns:
customer_id (Primary Key)
customer_name
email
phone
city
country
created_date
Table: ORDERS
Purpose: Stores customer orders.
Columns:
order_id (Primary Key)
customer_id (Foreign Key -> CUSTOMERS.customer_id)
order_date
amount
status
Table: PRODUCTS
product_id (Primary Key)
product_name
category
price
Table: ORDER_ITEMS
order_item_id (Primary Key)
order_id (Foreign Key)
product_id (Foreign Key)
quantity
unit_price
Tab

order_item_id (Primary Key)
order_id (Foreign Key)
product_id (Foreign Key)
quantity
unit_price
Table: EMPLOYEES
employee_id (Primary Key)
employee_name
department
manager_id (Self Foreign Key)
salary

hire_date

TABLE RELATIONSHIPS
CUSTOMERS 1 -> MANY ORDERS
ORDERS 1 -> MANY ORDER_ITEMS
PRODUCTS 1 -> MANY ORDER_ITEMS
EMPLOYEES.manager_id references EMPLOYEES.employee_id
Join Examples:
CUSTOMERS.customer_id = ORDERS.customer_id
ORDERS.order_id = ORDER_ITEMS.order_id
PRODUCTS.product_id = ORDER_ITEMS.product_id

BUSINESS RULES
Order status values:
Pending
Shipped
Delivered
Cancelled
A customer can have zero or many orders.
Each order belongs to one customer.
Amount stores total order value.
Prices are stored in PRODUCTS.price.

SQL GUIDELINES
Use ANSI SQL.
Use explicit JOIN syntax.
Never invent tables or columns.
Generate SQL only unless explanation is requested.
Use aliases for readability.
Prefer GROUP BY over subqueries when appropriate.

SAMPLE USER QUERIES
Show all customers from Bangalore.
List top 10 customers by total spending.
Show monthly sales.
Find products never ordered.
Find customers with no orders.
Find employees hired after 2024-01-01.
Average order amount by country.
Top selling products.
